Requirement: Verify that a named owner (role or team) is assigned responsibility for browser security policy and configuration across the organization
Verify that browser security responsibilities are documented across endpoint, identity, network, and application security functions with defined handoffs
Verify that browser risk is represented in the organization's risk register and reviewed on a defined cadence
Verify that an acceptable use policy covers browser usage, including sanctioned browsers, personal profile use, and extension installation
Verify that policy defines which browsers and versions are approved for business use, and prohibits unmanaged browsers for access to sensitive systems
Verify that policy addresses BYOD and unmanaged-device browser access to corporate resources, with technical enforcement defined
Verify that GenAI usage via the browser (chatbots, sidebars, agents) is covered by policy, including data classification rules for what may be submitted
Verify that a documented exception process exists for deviations from browser policy, with expiry dates and compensating controls
Verify that browser security policies and configurations are reviewed at least annually and after significant browser platform changes
Verify that browser controls are included in internal audit or independent assessment scope
Verify that security requirements (including this standard) are considered when procuring enterprise browsers, browser security tooling, or browser-based SaaS
Verify that third-party browser components (enterprise browsers, extension vendors) are covered by the organization's third-party risk process
Verify that the organization maintains an inventory of browsers (product and version) in use across managed endpoints
Verify that unmanaged or unapproved browsers on managed endpoints can be detected and remediated
Verify that browser access to sensitive applications from outside the managed fleet is identified (e.g., via IdP or application logs)
Verify that browser security settings are enforced centrally (e.g., via management policy) rather than relying on user-controlled defaults
Verify that enforced configuration is derived from a documented hardening baseline (e.g., CIS Benchmarks) with deviations recorded
Verify that users cannot disable or override security-relevant policies (e.g., Safe Browsing, extension controls, update settings)
Verify that configuration drift from the approved baseline is detected and alerted
Verify that automatic browser updates are enabled and cannot be disabled by users
Verify that browser versions across the fleet reach the latest stable release within a defined SLA, with reporting on laggards
Verify that a process exists for emergency deployment of browser patches for actively exploited vulnerabilities (0-days)
Verify that browser and extension vulnerabilities are included in the organization's vulnerability management program
Verify that relaunch/restart is enforced within a defined window after update download so patches take effect
Verify that unneeded high-risk browser capabilities (e.g., WebUSB, WebSerial, WebBluetooth, remote debugging) are disabled by policy where there is no business need
Verify that developer tools and browser flags are restricted on endpoints or for users where there is no business need
Verify that legacy or deprecated protocols and features (e.g., insecure TLS versions, deprecated plugin interfaces) are disabled fleet-wide
Verify that corporate browser profiles are separated from personal profiles, with corporate data confined to managed profiles
Verify that sync of corporate profile data (passwords, history, tabs) to personal accounts is blocked
Verify that high-risk browsing (unknown sites) can be isolated from sessions accessing sensitive applications (e.g., separate profiles, isolation technology)
Verify that users cannot install extensions from arbitrary or unofficial sources (sideloading, developer mode) on managed browsers
Verify that extension installation is restricted to an approved allowlist, or that a defined blocklist plus permission-based restrictions are enforced
Verify that extension installation requests follow a documented review-and-approval workflow
Verify that a documented process exists for assessing extensions before approval, covering permissions requested, publisher reputation, and data handling
Verify that extensions requesting high-risk permissions (e.g., access to all sites, reading browsing data, clipboard, native messaging) receive heightened review
Verify that approved extensions are re-assessed on ownership change, permission escalation, or a defined periodic cadence
Verify that installed extensions across the fleet are inventoried, including version and permission set
Verify that an extension can be force-removed or disabled fleet-wide within a defined SLA when found malicious or compromised
Verify that extension permission changes on update are detected and trigger re-review
Verify that extensions are blocked or restricted from running on designated sensitive sites (e.g., admin consoles, banking, healthcare records)
Verify that internally developed extensions follow secure development practices and are distributed through managed channels only
Verify that internally developed extensions undergo security review equivalent to other internal software before deployment
Verify that access to sensitive corporate applications through the browser requires SSO with MFA
Verify that phishing-resistant authentication (e.g., FIDO2/WebAuthn, passkeys) is deployed for high-value accounts and applications
Verify that authentication policies evaluate device and browser posture (managed state, browser version) before granting access to sensitive applications
Verify that session anomalies (token reuse from new device/location/IP) for critical applications are detected and can trigger revocation
Verify that session lifetimes and re-authentication requirements for sensitive applications are risk-appropriate and enforced
Verify that session credentials are bound to the device where supported (e.g., device-bound session credentials, token binding mechanisms), so exfiltrated cookies cannot be replayed elsewhere
Verify that administrative and privileged web sessions are conducted from hardened or isolated browser environments
Verify that an approved password manager is available to users, and policy defines whether the browser's built-in manager is sanctioned
Verify that browser-stored credentials are protected by OS-level encryption tied to the user account, and that saving corporate credentials into unsanctioned stores is restricted
Verify that credential autofill is restricted to exact-match, legitimate origins (mitigating phishing-site autofill)
Verify that corporate credentials cannot be entered into known-phishing or non-sanctioned lookalike sites (e.g., password reuse and paste detection for the corporate identity)
Verify that user consent to third-party OAuth applications for corporate identities is restricted or subject to admin approval
Verify that granted OAuth applications and scopes are periodically reviewed and stale or high-risk grants revoked
Verify that downloads from sensitive corporate applications to unmanaged devices or unsanctioned locations can be controlled
Verify that uploads of corporate data to unsanctioned destinations (personal cloud storage, file sharing, webmail) can be detected or blocked, based on data classification
Verify that transfers between corporate and personal contexts of the same service (e.g., corporate vs personal tenant of the same SaaS) are distinguished and controlled (tenant restrictions)
Verify that copy/paste of sensitive data from designated corporate applications to unsanctioned destinations can be restricted
Verify that printing and screen capture of designated sensitive web applications can be restricted where required by data classification
Verify that SaaS applications accessed through the browser are discoverable (shadow IT visibility), and access to unsanctioned categories can be controlled
Verify that a process exists to sanction, tolerate, or block newly discovered SaaS applications based on risk
Verify that submission of sensitive corporate data to unsanctioned GenAI services via the browser can be detected or blocked, consistent with policy (see 1.2.4)
Verify that controls distinguish sanctioned enterprise GenAI tenants from consumer versions of the same tools
Verify that browser-cached corporate data on shared or kiosk endpoints is cleared between users/sessions
Verify that corporate data in browser storage (cache, IndexedDB, service workers) on unmanaged devices is minimized or prevented for sensitive applications
Verify that reputation-based protection (e.g., Safe Browsing or equivalent) is enabled and enforced fleet-wide
Verify that enhanced or real-time URL protection is enabled for the fleet, with privacy implications assessed and documented
Verify that newly registered/observed domains and known AitM infrastructure indicators can be blocked at or before the browser
Verify that in-browser page analysis or equivalent controls detect credential-harvesting pages impersonating corporate identity providers
Verify that downloaded files are scanned by endpoint protection before execution
Verify that high-risk file types and password-protected archives from uncategorized sources are blocked or sandboxed by policy
Verify that social-engineering execution patterns delivered via the browser (e.g., copy-run-paste "ClickFix" instructions) are addressed by technical control and user awareness
Verify that HTTPS is required by default and users are warned or blocked on certificate errors, with error click-through disabled for managed fleets where feasible
Verify that DNS-over-HTTPS behavior is explicitly configured to align with enterprise DNS security controls rather than left to browser defaults
Verify that TLS inspection, where used, is scoped, documented, and excludes categories where inspection creates unacceptable privacy or legal risk
Verify that security awareness training includes browser-specific threats: consent phishing, fake updates, malicious extensions, MFA-bypass phishing
Verify that users have a low-friction way to report suspicious sites/pages encountered in the browser, and reports feed detection processes
Verify that AI-enabled browsers, sidebars, copilots, and agentic extensions in use are inventoried and classified as sanctioned or unsanctioned
Verify that policy defines which AI browsing capabilities are permitted, for which users, and with access to which data classes
Verify that unsanctioned AI browsers and agentic extensions can be technically blocked on managed endpoints
Verify that agentic capabilities cannot operate with access to authenticated corporate sessions unless explicitly sanctioned for that application

Verify that sanctioned agents operate under least privilege: scoped to defined sites/tasks, with sensitive actions (payments, permission changes, data export, sending communications) requiring human confirmation
Verify that agent sessions are distinguishable from human sessions in application and identity logs
Verify that the organization has assessed prompt-injection risk (page content or documents steering agent behavior) for each sanctioned agentic capability

Verify that mitigations exist for untrusted-content-driven agent actions (e.g., restricting agent browsing to trusted origins, isolating agent context from sensitive tabs, requiring confirmation for actions initiated after processing untrusted content)
Verify that data submitted to AI browser features is governed by the data protection controls in V5, including page-context capture by sidebars/copilots
Verify that sanctioned AI browsing features log actions taken and data accessed sufficiently to support incident investigation
Verify that AI browsing capabilities are included in incident response planning, including revoking agent access and investigating agent-performed actions
Verify that security-relevant browser events (extension installs, policy changes, malware/phishing blocks, dangerous downloads) are collected centrally
Verify that browser telemetry collection is documented, proportionate, and compliant with applicable employee privacy law and internal policy
Verify that telemetry covers data-movement events (uploads, downloads, paste to unsanctioned destinations) for sensitive data classes
Verify that browser telemetry is integrated with the organization's detection stack (SIEM/XDR) with defined alerting use cases
Verify that infostealer indicators (credential store access, mass cookie theft) on endpoints trigger revocation of browser sessions and credentials for affected users
Verify that incident response playbooks cover browser-layer scenarios: malicious extension, session token theft, AitM-phished credentials, data exfiltration via browser
Verify that browser artifacts needed for investigation (history, extension state, download records) can be acquired from managed endpoints
Verify that retention periods for browser telemetry meet investigation and regulatory needs
Verify that browser security posture metrics (patch latency, policy compliance, unapproved extension count, unmanaged browser usage) are reported to security leadership on a defined cadence
Verify that findings from browser-related incidents feed back into policy, configuration baselines, and this standard's local implementation
